items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with reflections on journeys and the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection

At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: 20th Anniversary of 48 Engineer Squadron, Waterloo
notes: Ron Ormson introduced Lieutenant Colonel Scott Burke, CD – Commanding Officer, 31 Combat Engineer Regiment (The Elgins) – Canadian Armed Forces Reserves; Chief Warrant Officer Art Churcher, CD; and Lieutenant Aaron Manory, CD.

Lieutenant Colonel Scott Burke, CD mentioned that it was an honor to recognize the 20th Anniversary of the reactivation of the 48th Engineer Field Squadron. He spoke about the history of the Squadron in Waterloo, and offered his thanks to the City for their support over the last 20 years.

Lieutenant Colonel Scott Burke, CD exchanged certificates with Mayor McCabe, gifting Mayor and Council with the “31 Combat Engineer Regiment (The Elgins) Commanding Officer’s Certificate of Appreciation”. He also presented Councillor Freeman with her Honorary Colonel Commissioning Scroll from Rideau Hall, signed by the Governor General and the Minister of Defence.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-05,
notes: Four Units Four Storeys, The Corporation
of the City of Waterloo, City Wide
Report No.: IPPW2024-045
Prepared By: Tristin Deveau and Adam Zufferli
Ward No.: All Wards

Tristin Deveau and Adam Zufferli gave a presentation outlining the proposed zoning by- law amendments, with some examples of existing built forms. They then responded to questions of Council. Joel Cotter also responded to questions of Council.
Tyler Ulmer, VP, Development, Cabinovo Housing gave a presentation in support of the proposed zoning by-law amendments, with some additional considerations.
Councillor Freeman left the Chair. (Time: 7:23 p.m.)
Councillor Bodaly in the Chair. (Time: 7:23 p.m.)
Councillor Bodaly left the Chair. (Time: 7:26 p.m.)
Councillor Freeman in the Chair. (Time: 7:26 p.m.)
Brooke Ashfield, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the importance of diversity and in favour of the proposed amendments.
Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed amendments.

Phil Marfisi, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the amendments, especially in relation to the housing crisis, the Housing Affordability Fund, and the Strategic Plan. He also spoke in favour of removing parking minimums.
Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the long-term impacts of maximum lot coverage, with about concerns regarding drainage and flooding. Ron Ormson responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application was open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Wright had a question for staff: Of the housing units currently in the pipeline, how many are one-bedroom? Ron Ormson responded that the Building Standards team would to compile that information.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer mentioned that Waterloo hosted 78 female hockey teams from across North America for the US-Canada Cup. During the competition, a hydro pole was hit and RIM Park lost power. She gave a shout-out to the customer service, security and custodial staff for acting with calmness and professionalism to ensure the safety and well-being of everyone in the facility, which also included a volleyball tournament at the same time. As a highlight, Canada won.

Councillor Wright mentioned the successful tree lighting in the Square on Friday, December 6. She mentioned that there was a lot of preparation to run those events, including getting the rink up and running. The BIA also ran markets on the weekend, and it was a tremendous effort.
Councillor Wright also gave a shoutout to the transportation team for work on winter control over the past weekend.

Councillor Roe mentioned that the Erb West Community Centre is hosting a holiday gift donation drive. You can reach out to Councillor Roe or Jordan at Erb West if you would like to participate. They are accepting donations to December 19 Councillor Vasic offered her thanks to recreation staff at the WMRC. They hosted a Provincial water polo championship on November 30-December 1.

Councillor Vasic also had a meeting with an advocacy group called, “Put Food Banks Out Of Business” last week, hosted by the Toronto Vegetarian Food Bank. They are planning to advocate in the next federal election for basic income.

Councillor Bodaly gave a shoutout to the Laurelwood Neighbourhood Association, who also hosted a tree lighting on Saturday, December 7, at Fire Station No. 2. He appreciates all of the help from volunteers and the folks at the fire station to host a really great event.

Councillor Freeman wanted to recognize December 6, the National Day of Remembrance and Action on Violence Against Women. There was a service in Ward 5, recognizing the 14 women who were killed 35 years ago, as well as Indigenous women and other women who find themselves in violence. She mentioned the extraordinary number of response calls that emergency services received this year, and that only 6% of individuals even make the phone call.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CORP2024-034. 2. That Council approve when the actual Enova Power Corp. dividend/investment income exceeds budget: • 50% of the surplus is transferred to the Capital Reserve Fund (CRF) • 25% of the surplus is transferred to the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund (CIRRF) • 25% of the surplus is transferred to the Climate Action Reserve Fund (CARF) 3. That Council approve the revised Employee Development and Capacity Building Reserve Fund policy attached as Appendix B. 4. That Council direct staff to include a recommended funding solution to address the projected declining balance of the Planning Litigation Reserve Fund, ensuring the Council Approved Funding Level is maintained, as a part of the 2024 Year End Surplus/Deficit Allocation report. 5. That Council approve the following administrative adjustments be updated in the Reserves and Reserve Funds Policies: a. That Council approve that all references to Council Approved Target Levels in the Reserve and Reserve fund policies be updated to Council Approved Funding Levels to avoid confusion, as individual reserve or reserve fund policies may outline a minimum, target, or cap level, or a combination of these levels. b. That Council approve that the vacancy savings calculation definition in the Sick Leave Reserve Fund Revenue policy be updated to 100% of the net difference between salary budget and actuals, less 50% of any calculated vacancy savings (position budget, less actuals, less labour-related commitments) for applicable positions, to align terminology with the revised EMPDV policy. c. That Council approve that the reference to an annual contribution from the Regional Municipality of Waterloo be removed from the Parking Reserve Fund revenue policy, due to the transfer of ownership of the Parkade and the revised governance agreement. d. That the Revenue Policy of the General Contingency Reserve be updated to reflect that the annual allocation of 10% of gross rent from City Centre leases occurs as a part of year-end processing. e. That the Council Approved Funding Level of the Building Permit Reserve Fund be updated to a target level of 18 months operating expenses and a minimum level of 12 months of operating expenses, to align with the Building Enterprise financial model. 6. That Council approve that FC-006 Reserves and Reserve Funds Policy, attached as Appendix C, be updated for the changes required through recommendations 1 through 5, inclusive.

3. That Council approve the revised Employee Development and Capacity Building Reserve Fund policy attached as Appendix B.

4. That Council direct staff to include a recommended funding solution to address the projected declining balance of the Planning Litigation Reserve Fund, ensuring the Council Approved Funding Level is maintained, as a part of the 2024 Year End Surplus/Deficit Allocation report.

5. That Council approve the following administrative adjustments be updated in the Reserves and Reserve Funds Policies: a. That Council approve that all references to Council Approved Target Levels in the Reserve and Reserve fund policies be updated to Council Approved Funding Levels to avoid confusion, as individual reserve or reserve fund policies may outline a minimum, target, or cap level, or a combination of these levels. b. That Council approve that the vacancy savings calculation definition in the Sick Leave Reserve Fund Revenue policy be updated to 100% of the net difference between salary budget and actuals, less 50% of any calculated vacancy savings (position budget, less actuals, less labour-related commitments) for applicable positions, to align terminology with the revised EMPDV policy. c. That Council approve that the reference to an annual contribution from the Regional Municipality of Waterloo be removed from the Parking Reserve Fund revenue policy, due to the transfer of ownership of the Parkade and the revised governance agreement. d. That the Revenue Policy of the General Contingency Reserve be updated to reflect that the annual allocation of 10% of gross rent from City Centre leases occurs as a part of year-end processing. e. That the Council Approved Funding Level of the Building Permit Reserve Fund be updated to a target level of 18 months operating expenses and a minimum level of 12 months of operating expenses, to align with the Building Enterprise financial model.

6. That Council approve that FC-006 Reserves and Reserve Funds Policy, attached as Appendix C, be updated for the changes required through recommendations 1 through 5, inclusive.
